title: Selby St James Halifax Memorial
location_name: St James Church, New Lane, Selby, North Yorkshire
memorial_type: Metal plaque on the nave wall, shown with flags and the spire's cockerel
memorial_details: A metal plaque on the nave wall at St James Church, Selby, records the strike and the church's restoration, and is shown with British and Australian flags and the spire's cockerel. Yorkshire Aircraft says a memorial plaque was unveiled in the church on 1 November 1953 and that a 70th anniversary service was held there in 2014. The church was re-dedicated on 11 December 1950 and the tower was rebuilt without a spire.
narrative: Halifax JB789 of 1658 Heavy Conversion Unit was on a circuits and landings exercise from Riccall. It took off for its third circuit at 01.00 and struck the spire of St James Church, Selby, at 01.02 on 10 May 1944. It came down across Portholme Road and Union Lane, through the roof of Portholme Mill and onto Portholme Drive. All seven aircrew were killed. The inquiry reached no firm conclusion. The sources give different totals for civilian dead, so the number is not settled here.
cause_of_loss: Failed to gain height on take-off and struck the spire of St James Church; the inquiry reached no firm conclusion
community_connection: The church website refers to a WWII display in the church.

external_narratives.summary: IWM entry for a metal plaque on the wall in the south west corner of the nave of St James Church, Selby. It records the 1944 spire strike and the church's restoration and re-dedication, and says the plaque is shown with British and Australian flags and the spire's golden cockerel. It names no maintainer.
key_details: Plaque states aircraft struck the spire on 10 May 1944

external_narratives.summary: The parish church's own page says a Halifax returning from training crashed into the spire in 1944, killing all seven crew and six local residents, and that the tower was rebuilt without a spire. It does not mention the plaque and does not say who maintains it.
key_details: Seven crew and six residents killed (church figure)
Tower rebuilt without a spire

external_narratives.summary: Gives the crash only as May 1944, with the crew and eight people in nearby houses killed. Cites The Press, 19 March 2014, which was not readable.
key_details: Crew and eight residents killed
